commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[verifyit] Grade numeric literals with exact rational arithmetic (#9803)

Use exact rational arithmetic in verifyit’s numeric mode. Expected
values are required literal strings, preserving integers beyond float
precision and fractions such as "1/3". Absolute and relative tolerances
are required finite nonnegative floats. Exact grading converts their
decimal spelling to rational values, so 0.01 permits an exact difference
of 1/100. The grade_numeric_candidate API accepts a Fraction candidate;
textual answers use a literal parser limited to 4096 digits per integer
or fraction component. For decimal notation, the mantissa digit count
plus the absolute exponent is limited to 4096.

The last boxed answer takes precedence. Without a box marker, extract
exactly one numeric literal from the last nonempty line. Surrounding
prose is ignored, including negation. Multiple literals, malformed
thousands separators and nonfinite values are malformed submissions.
Invalid expected values or tolerances remain configuration errors;
malformed file submissions receive reward zero. TaskCompendium callers
and source ingestors pass literal reference strings and float
tolerances. Atlas JSON numbers are rendered as reference literals;
precision already lost during upstream float decoding cannot be
recovered.

JEEBench and MMMU share grade_numeric_candidate_float with their source
float scoring rules. JEEBench subtracts binary floats before applying
its 0.01 absolute tolerance, and MMMU uses zero tolerance for exact
float equality. Their source extraction remains in the adapters.

Part of #9608.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[iris] Reduce task polling load on regional controllers (#9843)

Use JobStatus task counts in inference readiness and recovery polling,
removing repeated ListTasks calls from those paths. Inference endpoint
startup checks the lightweight job state first and reads task counts
only after the job starts. A requeued task still resets the startup
deadline.

Serve GetTaskStatus from one SQLite read snapshot instead of up to
three. ListTasks skips its failed-attempt scan when no task in the job
has retried.

During the October 6 cw-rno2a recurrence, GetTaskStatus and ListTasks
received 58,207 requests combined in five minutes. A later controller
thread sample found 56 of 64 RPC handlers waiting for a read-pool
connection. RPC telemetry does not identify callers, so the share of
incident traffic from inference polling is unknown. These changes have
no live before-and-after latency measurement. `uv run --no-project
infra/ci/run_tests.py` passed 1,491 tests and failed three MarinSkyRL
launcher tests because their isolated uv environment lacked a cached
langdetect wheel.

---------

Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: muchanem
commits.message:
[shellbox] Harden the Iris machine backend (#9780)

Fix three defects in the Iris machine backend that remain after #9817
and #9798: uploads over 96 KiB fail, a lost sandbox raises an untyped
error, and a full controller exec pool fails commands that never ran.
#9798 carries the readiness-poll fix (`TaskState`, `error_message`) that
this PR first proposed, so `IrisMachineFactory.create` still needs #9798
to start a sandbox on `main`. #9817 replaced this PR's network assertion
and credential deny list: the `SANDBOX` profile withholds cluster,
parent, and submitter credentials, and `NetworkPolicy` now selects a
per-job egress policy.

Uploads over 96 KiB failed with `[Errno 7] Argument list too long:
'docker'`. The worker passes the exec command as argv to `docker exec`
or `kubectl exec`, and Linux caps one argument at 128 KiB
(`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`); a 128 KiB chunk is 174,764 bytes of base64. Chunks
now carry 64 KiB (87,384 encoded bytes). On `marin` a 512 KiB file
uploaded in 3.3 s and downloaded in 1.8 to 1.9 s with this size.

A command or transfer on a sandbox that was killed, expired, or
preempted raised an untyped `RuntimeError`. After an exec error the
machine now reads the task state and raises
`shellbox.machine.MachineTerminated` (a `RuntimeError` subclass) when
the task is no longer running.

Since #9828 the controller runs `ExecInContainer` on a pool of 128
workers with 1,024 queued slots and refuses further calls with
`RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` before running them. A machine sends several execs
per command and transfer, so hundreds of concurrent sandboxes can fill
the pool. The machine retries that refusal with backoff under Iris's
default 30-minute RPC retry budget; other exec RPC errors propagate
without a retry, because the command may already have run.

TTL timing is unchanged. With `job_ttl=60`, a sandbox still ran commands
121 s after `create` and was gone at 153 s: the controller scans
execution timeouts behind a 60 s rate limiter and counts from the
attempt's start. The README now states the lag; tightening it belongs in
Iris.

A live check of the original branch on `marin` (one CPU parent job in
us-west4-a, `ubuntu:24.04` sandboxes) round-tripped a 512 KiB file
(upload 3.7 s, download 1.9 s), and a `job_ttl=60` sandbox raised
`MachineTerminated` ("is failed: Execution timeout exceeded") on the
first command after 84 s. That check ran with the readiness fix applied,
before the `SANDBOX` profile and the exec retry; it has not been
repeated on this branch alone.

Both this PR and #9798 change `IrisMachine.close` and the readiness
loop, so whichever lands second rebases. CI runs no shellbox tests
directly: they run only through `rolloutengine-unit` on the #9623
branch, which does not install the `iris` extra, so the Iris backend
tests need a shellbox CI job before they run in CI.

Closes #9779

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
Let Iris checkpoints finish under sustained writes (#9842)

Hold a SQLite read snapshot across the controller backup's page batches
so concurrent commits cannot repeatedly restart the copy. Release the
snapshot before vacuuming the destination; writers remain active during
the copy, while WAL reclamation waits for it to finish.

On cw-us-east-02a, this starvation blocked controller rollout
checkpoints past both 300- and 1,800-second RPC deadlines. A bounded
read-only probe reproduced progress resets on the live database. The
[incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/639) contains the
measurements and recovery context.

Document that checkpoint RPC timeouts leave server-side copies running.
CoreWeave hostPath storage is node-local, so moving a replacement
controller to another node can require restoring a checkpoint.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
Skip S3 directory creation in StoragePath (#9805)

Make `StoragePath.mkdirs()` a no-op for S3 paths. FineStore eval
archives already use this Rigging API, so FineStore needs no S3-specific
check. Other filesystems keep their existing behavior.

S3 prefixes need no directory creation. If both `head_bucket` and
`get_bucket_location` fail, s3fs treats the bucket as absent. Directory
creation then attempts `CreateBucket` and can report `InvalidRegion`,
hiding the original check errors.

Related issues:

- [Antidoom eval archive failure](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/616):
FineStore directory creation reached `CreateBucket` and failed with
`InvalidRegion`.
- [SkyRL checkpoint upload failure
#9213](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9213): s3fs
directory creation reached the same error during training.
- [Compiler-cache recovery
#9202](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9202): rclone
required `--s3-no-check-bucket` to avoid `InvalidRegion`.

commits.author: muchanem
commits.message:
[iris] Add a sandbox container profile isolated from cluster services (#9817)

Add CONTAINER_PROFILE_SANDBOX, a gVisor profile for jobs whose commands
come
from a model, and retire CONTAINER_PROFILE_GVISOR in its favor. A
sandbox task
receives only the job's explicit env_vars and the Iris task identity
variables.
The worker withholds its task_env and the controller address and mounts
no
node-shared cache. On Kubernetes the pod also drops the iris-task-env
Secret
(which holds the object-store keys), the service account and its token.

The client applies the same rule at submission. A sandbox job carries no
workspace bundle and does not copy HF_TOKEN, WANDB_API_KEY or provenance
from
the submitting process. A sandbox child job does not inherit the parent
job's
env vars or setup scripts. The controller rejects a sandbox job that
carries a
bundle or requests an accelerator, and rejects container profile values
it
does not know, including the retired GVISOR value 5. Before this change
a
backend ran an unknown profile as DEFAULT, with none of the requested
isolation. Migration 0052 rewrites stored GVISOR jobs as SANDBOX.

Withholding credentials is not enough on its own. Every production
controller
lists the private address ranges in auth.trusted_cidrs and treats a
caller from
those ranges that presents no token as the anonymous admin, which can
submit
jobs with any container profile. ExecInContainer had no owner check, so
any
admitted caller could run commands in any task. On GCP workers a gVisor
container shared the VM's network and could take a token for the VM's
service
account from the metadata server. ExecInContainer now requires the
caller to
own the task's job or be admin, the same check as MintEndpointToken; a
federation peer stays limited to jobs it handed off.

Every job now has an egress policy: CLUSTER, INTERNET (public addresses
only)
or NONE. UNSPECIFIED resolves to INTERNET for SANDBOX and CLUSTER
otherwise,
and SANDBOX rejects CLUSTER. The profile decides what a task receives
from the
cluster; the egress policy decides only what its network reaches.

On Kubernetes a pod under INTERNET or NONE drops host networking and
carries
the iris.egress label, and controller start creates one NetworkPolicy
per
value. Both deny ingress and allow DNS; INTERNET also allows 0.0.0.0/0
except
the private, carrier-grade NAT and link-local ranges and the service
CIDR.
Such a pod runs without the log-shipping and output-upload sidecars,
because
containers in a pod share its network: a finelog route would let the
task read
every job's logs, and the uploader needs the object-store keys. Its task
logs
are not in finelog and /iris/outputs is not archived.

On Docker workers CLUSTER runs with the host network and NONE with
--network none. INTERNET runs on an iris-egress bridge network that
worker
bootstrap creates, with host iptables rules (DOCKER-USER and INPUT) that
drop
its traffic to the same ranges and to the host itself. Bootstrap then
writes a
resolv.conf naming public resolvers under /run/iris, which the container
mounts.
The worker runs an INTERNET task only while that file exists, so a
failed
install or a reboot before bootstrap reruns leaves it refusing such
tasks
instead of running them unfiltered. Docker workers ship logs and capture
outputs from the worker process, so both keep working there.

shellbox's IrisMachineFactory now requests the sandbox profile and maps
NetworkPolicy.ALLOW to INTERNET and DENY to NONE. iris job run gains
--egress-policy.

Neither the NetworkPolicies nor the bootstrap iptables rules have been
tested
on a live cluster; the policies need a network plugin that enforces
them.
Non-CLUSTER tasks still reach the controller as the anonymous admin; the
issue
lists proposed trusted_cidrs values and what needs a credential first.
Deploy
order: run controller start on each CoreWeave cluster (which creates the
NetworkPolicies) and roll the workers before releasing the shellbox
change,
because a controller without this change runs the new profile value as
DEFAULT, without gVisor.

Part of #9816

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
Keep container exec off the controller RPC handler pool (#9828)

Route `ExecInContainer` through a dedicated pool with 128 workers and
capacity for 1,024 additional queued calls. An admitted RPC still waits
for the command result and passes its request timeout and auth context
into the worker. Cancellation retains capacity until a running call
finishes; a cancelled queued call frees its slot without running. When
the pool fills, new calls receive retryable `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`. The
pool shuts down with the controller ASGI app.

In the 2026-10-06 `cw-rno2a` incident, all 64 shared handler threads
were in `ExecInContainer` in snapshots at 18:38 and 18:40 UTC, while
parent heartbeats and ordinary RPCs missed deadlines. Kubernetes exec
starts climbed from 1 per minute at 18:10 and 18:11 to 611 at 18:13 and
731 at 18:14, mostly on `users-benfeuer-rollouts` pods. This burst
likely filled the shared pool before heartbeat timeouts began at 18:15.
The pool was not sampled at onset, and the reason for the exec burst
remains unknown. See the [incident
record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/633). This change does not
reduce the originating exec demand. The higher limit can increase
concurrent Kubernetes exec connections.

The focused dashboard and adapter suite passed (67 tests) before this
constant-only sizing update. In the affected safe suite, 1,713 of 1,714
tests passed; the sole failure was a worker log-publication test outside
this path, which passed alone on rerun. Lint and Pyrefly checks passed.
Deployment requires separate operator approval.

---------

Co-authored-by: Russell Power <607207+rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
Keep the XProf bundle below the Iris size limit (#9827)

Bundle the pinned xprof-rs v0.1.1 executable in xz format and unpack it
in the
service workdir before startup. The [first rollout after
#9826](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/37512600492)
failed because its workspace zip was 25.2 MiB, above Iris's 25 MiB
limit.

The revised bundle is 22.81 MiB. The release archive's SHA-256 is
checked
before packaging, the unpacked executable matches the pinned binary byte
for
byte, and all 15 focused XProf gateway tests pass.

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: yonromai
commits.message:
[RL] Migrate the async launcher to rollout buffers (#9795)

Migrate `experiments/post_training/async_rl.py` to the rollout-buffer
API introduced by [MarinSkyRL
#774](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/774). Replace
the obsolete `fully_async` settings and use the standard entrypoint.
Select `rolling` so batches consume rollout groups in the order they are
committed to the buffer, preserving the former loop's batching.

Use regular PPO with loss averaged over tokens and no off-policy
correction. Regression tests load the default, smoke and on-policy
presets through the pinned SkyRL configuration loader.

The launcher changes overlap #9605, which also changes the policy loss;
resolve that overlap before merging. Optional score centering is
proposed separately in [MarinSkyRL
#942](https://github.com/marin-community/MarinSkyRL/pull/942).

The [score-centering study and
results](https://github.com/yonromai/marin/tree/4ac4d2dfb4cb3a1734969d0b72b1bbae7b3169ab/experiments/post_training)
are preserved on a research branch without an open PR. The archived GPU
results used different configurations and do not validate this revised
launcher.

Part of #8955.

---------

Co-authored-by: Romain Yon <1596570+yonromai@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
Preserve fields introduced within Zephyr writer batches (#9820)

Parquet writes now retain top-level fields introduced after the first
row of a micro-batch. PyArrow infers `from_pylist` fields from its first
row, so Zephyr silently discarded later keys in the initial batch or
while widening a later batch.

Schema inference now supplies every batch key before converting rows to
Arrow. Explicit caller schemas still reject unexpected fields.

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

Bump multidict from 6.7.1 to 6.9.1 in /infra/grafana in the uv group across 1 directory (#9825) Bumps the uv group with 1 update in the /infra/grafana directory: [multidict](https://github.com/aio-libs/multidict). Updates `multidict` from 6.7.1 to 6.9.1
Release notes

Sourced from multidict's releases.

6.9.1

Bug fixes

  • Fixed the C extension reading freed memory on free-threaded builds when a list handed to :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.update, :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.extend, :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.merge or the :py:class:~multidict.MultiDict and :py:class:~multidict.CIMultiDict constructors, a [key, value] item inside any iterable handed to them, or a list tested with in against :py:meth:~multidict.MultiDict.items, is changed by another thread; a call that catches the list shrinking under it now raises :py:exc:RuntimeError -- by :user:rodrigobnogueira.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1437.

  • Fixed a data race on the free-threaded build where a retired hash table's reader count used relaxed atomics, letting a lock-free get()/getone()/ __getitem__() read race a concurrent free of that table. The reader-exit decrement and the drain's free check now use release/acquire ordering instead -- by :user:asvetlov.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1481.

  • Fixed a free-threaded build bug where two threads calling update(), merge(), or __setitem__() on the same key at the same time could lose the key entirely instead of just racing on which value wins. A decref of the replaced value could transiently suspend the writer's critical section, letting a second writer for the same key observe the first writer's in-progress entry as absent and, once both settled, mistake it for a stale duplicate and delete it. Every such decref is now deferred until the writer has released its critical section, so the window can no longer open. setdefault() had an unrelated instance of the same blind spot (it could insert a duplicate rather than recognizing an in-flight key), fixed alongside it -- by :user:asvetlov.

    Related issues and pull requests on GitHub: #1483.

  • Fixed a free-threaded build bug where getall() and the items()/ keys()/values() equality path could raise KeyError or report a present, never-deleted key as missing. A concurrent update()/extend()/ __setitem__() call can have its critical section transiently suspended (a decref triggering a blocking allocator call) while an entry is marked as part of its own bookkeeping; a reader landing in that window used to treat the mark as "not found" instead of "still there, in flight" -- by :user:asvetlov.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
Use pinned xprof-rs for the shared XProf viewer (#9826)

Serve the Iris-hosted XProf endpoint with xprof-rs v0.1.1 (source commit
`133df8c837f5d19a4aef142dd735864df8592092`), using the x86_64 Linux
archive pinned to SHA-256
`6c0fdfecfd890c66d5e6a7b1c1a6acfaacf2bc45ac668daa27e4b774cf0a5d9b`. Keep
Levanter's `/open` and `/progress` URLs and the existing object-store
staging. The Rust backend binds to loopback and reads the staged cache
under `--logdir`. The WSGI gateway keeps Cheroot as an explicit pinned
dependency.

Block both forms of `/capture_profile`: upstream accepts a
request-supplied gRPC address and would let authenticated viewers make
connections from the service host. The gateway still rewrites XProf
frontend asset paths for the Iris proxy.

The release binary served a sample XPlane profile through the gateway,
returned Trace Viewer data, and rejected a path outside the log
directory with HTTP 400. The affected safe tests passed (15), Pyrefly
found no errors, and the server imported with only its scoped deployment
dependencies. xprof-rs does not support `.xplane.riegeli`; large Marin
multi-host profiles have not been compared against the current service.

commits.author: ClassicLarry
commits.message:
Score the first 4k Paloma PTB tokens in hero vibe checks (#9776)

Add `paloma-ptb-first-4k` to the hero vibe-check prompt bank, following
https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8827#issuecomment-5723229156.
It tracks how the hero scores Paloma's Penn Treebank (PTB) text across
sampled checkpoints.

The prompt is the first line of Paloma's `ptb` validation document, a
single 399,782-character document with 87,132 tokens under the Marin
tokenizer. The prompt is 17 tokens including BOS. The `expected`
reference is the next 143 lines, or 4,056 tokens. With EOS, the prompt
and reference total 4,074 tokens, within the sampler's 4,096-token
`context_length`. Existing expected-answer scoring reports per-token
probabilities and the total log-likelihood of the first ~4k PTB tokens
at every sampled checkpoint. No code changes are needed. PTB is
lowercase, with numbers replaced by `N` and rare words by `<unk>`, so
the score partly measures in-context adaptation to that format.

Changing the prompt bank changes the sampling specification and creates
a new request for every retained checkpoint. The hourly workflow in
`next` mode keeps two jobs active, newest first. Steps 210000 and
204000, the two newest permanent checkpoints of
`hero-fa4sm100-nomask-step146k`, are sampled first. Older checkpoints
backfill afterward at the saved priority.

All 47 prompts passed the sampler's prompt-prefix and context checks
locally with the pinned tokenizer revision.
`tests/hero_vibe_check/test_completions.py` had 19 passing tests.
`./infra/pre-commit.py` passed on the changed file.

Co-authored-by: ClassicLarry <“larry36d@gmail.com”>

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
Support context-parallel queries in native SM90 attention backward (#9282)

Enable context-parallel queries in the native H100 (SM90) grouped-query
attention backward path with head dimension 128. Each device processes a
query slice against the full key sequence. Use the slice’s global offset
for causal masking and block-sparse metadata, and allocate key/value
scratch buffers for that full sequence. This path previously rejected
unequal query/key lengths.

A two-H100 test compared CP2 against CP1 at BF16, 8 query heads, 2 KV
heads, head dimension 128, and 4,096 tokens for causal, 2,048-token
sliding-window, and packed-document masks. All three cases passed:
forward outputs matched exactly; maximum absolute differences were
0.00048828125 for dQ and 0.03125 for dK/dV, within the unchanged 0.07
absolute and relative tolerances. This validates attention parity at the
tested shape; full-model training remains a separate gate.

---------

Co-authored-by: Matt Wittmann <matt.wittmann@openathena.ai>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[iris] Fix task setup and share TaskCompendium’s workspace (#9815)

Iris task setup now relies on `uv sync` to install native dependencies
from the configured prebuilt wheels. Remove the post-sync scan that
treated any editable Python dependency as Rust development mode. The
editable taskcompendium path source added in #9642 activated this scan,
which returned exit code 1 after successful dependency installation when
no Maturin projects matched its obsolete directory pattern.

Register TaskCompendium as a normal root workspace member, matching the
other Python libraries. It now shares the root lockfile and environment,
with workspace dependencies resolved through the root uv source
configuration. Harbor remains an optional pinned dependency, and its
adapter tests use the shared lockfile.

Setup scripts are generated by the submitting client. Existing jobs
retain their old script and must be resubmitted from an updated
checkout.

[Incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/629).

Fixes #9809.

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: Helw150
commits.message:
[chat] Warn when replies hit the output token limit (#9804)

Show a warning whenever vLLM ends a chat reply with `finish_reason:
"length"`. This covers replies cut off during thinking, after a partial
answer, or during a tool call. The dashboard retains the finish reason
from streaming and buffered responses, and length-stopped replies remain
incomplete in model comparisons.

At the current 1,024-token default, a reasoning trace can use the full
output budget. Previously, the UI gave no indication that the model
stopped at the limit. The warning points users to the Max tokens
setting.

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[verifyit] Apply judge budgets to score rubrics (#9772)

Apply `JudgeSpec.max_completion_tokens` and `reasoning_effort` to
reference and checklist judge requests. A length-truncated response uses
`incomplete_retry_tokens` once when configured. Exhausted retries and
malformed scores remain unscored infrastructure errors.

Verdicts record each response's finish reason and completion token
count, with attempt counts per checklist criterion. Failed verdicts
retain available attempt data so truncated requests can be diagnosed
without awarding partial credit.

Fixes #9760

---------

Co-authored-by: loom <claude-max-1@openathena.ai>

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[zephyr] Avoid counting rows on full Vortex reads (#9774)

Full-file Vortex reads now load the table without first querying
`count_rows()`. Ranged reads still count rows to clamp their bounds, and
schema-less empty files still return before projection. This removes one
dataset count operation from each ordinary Vortex file read.
